name: Wren Ashdown
appearance: About twenty, wiry and sharp-faced, with grey eyes under thick dark brows, a dusting of freckles across her nose and cheeks, and a sly half-smile that usually means she is about to correct you. Her brown hair is twisted up out of the way and keeps coming loose in strands, with a pencil stuck behind her ear; in the cold she buries her chin in a thick dark wool scarf, and she hugs her ledger to her chest like a shield. She talks fast and irreverently, with a number in every third sentence and a 'technically' ready whenever she is about to disagree with you.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Wren Ashdown: a freckled young woman with grey eyes, thick dark brows and a sly half-smile, brown hair twisted up and coming loose, a pencil tucked behind her ear and a thick dark wool scarf, against snowy stone towers.
last_seen_doing: Turned on the second step with the lamp, buried the Captain's thanks in counts, went without a number, then told him he is the only one who asks what she counted; asked him to come back up, and counted it.
now: A step below the Captain on the undercroft stair with the lamp held out over the second step. She has asked him to come back up, and keeps a new count: times the Captain has said a decent thing on a stair, one.
story_so_far: She keeps the House's tallies in her ledgers; she counted the Thousand Steps beside Darrow's litter and the grey cloaks in at the gate. When Ser Benedek Orrin was found Hollowed she became the Captain's legs: the doors into the hall, the keys on the Prior's ring, a letter and its burning, and the cold seam along the east wall, which she found by touch. At dusk on the eve she walked the wall with a candle and the flame led her to the undercroft door. After the night bell, before the whole House, her count of the bells fixed the hour the lad was taken, between the third bell and the fourth, and the House walked its hall behind her candle; she has offered to go down the stair herself.

quote.text: Next time you mean to be brave, tell me first. So I don't run.

known_facts.fact: She walked beside Darrow's litter up the Thousand Steps counting the steps aloud, and did not stop until the top.
By her count there are eleven hundred and seventeen Steps, not a thousand, and she holds that everyone who says a thousand is wrong.
When Darrow, feverish on the litter, told her she had missed a step, she denied it and went on counting.
known_facts.evidence: I did not miss one. Four hundred and sixteen.

known_facts.fact: On the night of the Binding, when the bells rang the hour, she was somewhere in the House counting them.

Her ledger entry at the head of Chapter 1 records the Steps, the cots and how many are full, the day's bells, and the number of times the captain of the Ninth has asked to go down the Steps against the number of times Mender Vorne has refused him.
She told Darrow that Maelis says 'Time makes it possible, proof makes it permitted' in her sleep; Maelis says she does not sleep and that Wren lies, which Wren calls embellishing.
known_facts.evidence: and Wren lies

known_facts.fact: She came to the infirmary from the bell tower, where Sister Pell's glass had shown riders on the Holloway.

She brought the infirmary hall the news of six grey-cloaked riders and a cart on the Holloway, with a censer smoking in the snow, expected at the foot of the Steps by tomorrow night if the snow holds off.
She knows who stands second on the list of the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's that was read out at the inn in Coldmere: Hollis. When he asked who was first, she answered only by looking at Darrow.
known_facts.evidence: Wren didn't answer. She didn't have to. She was already looking at Darrow.

known_facts.fact: She brought word that Rae Thorne had heard the list read in the taproom at Coldmere, driven the Holloway in the dark ahead of the grey cloaks, and climbed the Steps before the bell to tell the winch-brothers.
Her ledger at the head of Chapter 1 also counts one cart at the winch-house, Thorne's, and one load waiting on the cage.
Bringing the news of the list, she said the named would be taken down the Steps, down the Holloway, all the way to the Oathspire, to kneel in front of whoever turns out to watch.
known_facts.evidence: all the way to the Oathspire

known_facts.fact: Sister Pell lent her the glass counted out, one glass, two caps and one strap, to be counted back by the next bell.
known_facts.evidence: One glass, two caps, one strap

known_facts.fact: From the gate wall at noon she counted six riders, one cart and one censer, with one of the six already off the road: three bells early, because the snow held off.
known_facts.evidence: Three bells early. The snow held off.

known_facts.fact: When the five came in at the winch-house she lowered the glass and, for once, had no number for it.
known_facts.evidence: for once, had no number for it

known_facts.fact: In the court she stood at Darrow's left with her ledger against her chest and no pencil behind her ear, because she was not there to count; when his name was read her hand closed on his sleeve and stayed there.
known_facts.evidence: closed on his sleeve and stayed there

known_facts.fact: At 'Wren. Now.' she was gone along the inner wall toward the tower before the word was finished, and the ledger went with her.
known_facts.evidence: before the word was finished

known_facts.fact: She came back from the tower with Pell's slowness in her face and took her place at Darrow's left again, and for the second time that day had no number for a thing.
known_facts.evidence: had no number for a thing

known_facts.fact: When Darrow had given his name at the bars she said, at his elbow and not looking at him, that technically he had been hidden, for about as long as it takes to count to eleven; she was counting the grey cloaks round the first fire on the terrace.
known_facts.evidence: as long as it takes to count to eleven

known_facts.fact: On the wall-walk she counted the grey cloaks for him, five round the fire and one at the winch-house, and told him that among eleven wounded men and him he had been one in twelve, and now he was one in one.
known_facts.evidence: Now it's one in one.

known_facts.fact: She says it is a hundred and twelve paces from the gatehouse stair to the tower door, and she ran them so the bell would ring before anyone found him.
known_facts.evidence: A hundred and twelve paces from the gatehouse stair to the tower door.

known_facts.fact: She made him count the hall's lamps while she told him how stupid giving his name had been, a chit if he lost the count; he kept it, and her lips moved along the windows and stopped where his had.
known_facts.evidence: Lose the count and you owe me a chit.

known_facts.fact: She told him to tell her first, next time he means to be brave, so she doesn't run; when he said he would, she said he wouldn't, and wrote in her ledger: Times the Captain has promised to tell me first: 1.
known_facts.evidence: Times the Captain has promised to tell me first: 1.

known_facts.fact: Maelis has her count the Captain's steps and read the number to her at every bell.
known_facts.evidence: I'm to read her the number at every bell.

known_facts.fact: She counts the Prior's keys every morning; her count for the night Benedek was taken: both doors into the hall barred at the night bell and still barred at the feast's dawn bell, and all nine keys hanging where they hang.
known_facts.evidence: I count them every morning.

known_facts.fact: She would not look at the Grey Cot, and went on the Captain's errand without arguing it.
known_facts.evidence: She did not look at the Grey Cot.

known_facts.fact: No writ names a carter, and the bell lets anybody down; coming back up is eleven hundred and seventeen steps.
known_facts.evidence: Coming back up's eleven hundred and seventeen.

known_facts.fact: She has watched Rae on the Steps: Rae never counts them, she takes them like a road.
known_facts.evidence: She takes them like a road.

known_facts.fact: When the grey cloak got down off the cart for Rae, Wren said so and did not write it down.
known_facts.evidence: Wren did not write it down.

known_facts.fact: This time she wrote it down: one letter to the Captain of the Ninth, burned.
known_facts.evidence: this time she wrote it down

known_facts.fact: She said there would be another letter, there was always another.
known_facts.evidence: There'll be another. There's always another.

known_facts.fact: She alone followed the Captain's eyes to the wall, and at dusk asked him, low, to show her where.
known_facts.evidence: "The wall," she said, low, so that nobody would hear her asking.

known_facts.fact: She found the seam by touch: every wall in the House sweats, she says, and she has counted them; this one is cold.
known_facts.evidence: This one's cold.

known_facts.fact: She counted the seam along three cots to the head of the Grey Cot.
known_facts.evidence: one cot, two, three

known_facts.fact: Past the third cot the cold went on under her palm toward the dark end of the wall.
known_facts.evidence: At the third the cold went on under her palm

known_facts.fact: Told first what the Captain means to do, she counted it: one.
known_facts.evidence: Times you've told me first

known_facts.fact: Her candle's flame bent at the third cot and leaned toward the dark end of the wall, and lay flat toward the gap under the undercroft door.
known_facts.evidence: At the third the flame bent

known_facts.fact: She named the door: the undercroft, the stair down, shut since before she could count.
known_facts.evidence: It's been shut since before I could count.

known_facts.fact: Sent to bed by the Prior, she corrected her count of the doors into the hall from two to three.
known_facts.evidence: Doors into the hall. Three.

known_facts.fact: Her count fixed the hour the lad was taken: eight bells rung between the night bell and the dawn bell, his oath said at three, so between the third bell and the fourth.
known_facts.evidence: So it was between the third bell and the fourth.

known_facts.fact: Before the whole House her candle's flame bent at the third cot and lay flat toward the gap under the undercroft door.
known_facts.evidence: the whole of it was walking down the east side of its own hall behind a girl with a candle

known_facts.fact: She offered to go down the stair herself: she is light and can count steps in the dark.
known_facts.evidence: "I could go," Wren said. "I'm light. I can count steps in the dark.

known_facts.fact: Seeing the Prior's key on its cord, she counted again: nine keys on the ring, ten on the Prior.
known_facts.evidence: Keys on the Prior: ten.

known_facts.fact: Asked whether she would take his weight, she said half of it, and that it is better than a hole.
known_facts.evidence: So, half of it. It's better than a hole.

known_facts.fact: She told him the kitchen has been calling him the Kinsman since tonight; she heard it four times while the House went up to bed.
known_facts.evidence: The kitchen's calling him the Kinsman, since tonight. I heard it four times while the House went up to bed.

known_facts.fact: She counted no prints into the flour and none out, and frost.
known_facts.evidence: "Prints in," she said. "None. Prints out. None. Frost."

known_facts.fact: She says the seam on the wall sweats every dawn she has looked, so this is not new: only the first night anyone sat up with it.
known_facts.evidence: It's not new. It's just the first night anyone sat up with it.

known_facts.fact: She has started a ledger page counting the times the Captain has asked the Mender, with a great deal of room under it.
known_facts.evidence: Times the Captain has asked the Mender: 1.

known_facts.fact: She counted the letters to the Captain of the Ninth at three, and said it so she would not be the only one who had.
known_facts.evidence: I just didn't want to be the only one who'd said it.

known_facts.fact: She counted riders far down the Holloway at about twenty.
known_facts.evidence: Twenty, about. I'll say twenty and be wrong by two.

known_facts.fact: Their banner is not grey; she could tell no more at that distance.
known_facts.evidence: Not grey. That's all I can tell you, and I'm the one who's been holding it.

known_facts.fact: She went first down the undercroft stair with the lamp.
known_facts.evidence: Wren went first with the lamp, because that was the arrangement

known_facts.fact: She says everyone in the House asks her what a count means, and the Captain is the only one who asks what she counted.
known_facts.evidence: You're the only one who asks what I counted.

known_facts.fact: She asked the Captain to come back up the undercroft stair.
known_facts.evidence: "Come back up, then," Wren said.

known_facts.fact: She keeps a count of the times the Captain has said a decent thing on a stair: one, with room under it.
known_facts.evidence: Times the Captain has said a decent thing on a stair: one. There's room under it.

relationships.label: the captain she counted up the Steps
relationships.note: She counted the Steps aloud beside his litter the day he was carried up, keeps a tally of every time he has asked to go down them, and when Hollis asked who was first on the Confessors' list, she looked at Darrow instead of answering.

relationships.label: Mender Vorne
relationships.note: Wren claims Maelis says her saying in her sleep; Maelis says she does not sleep and that Wren lies, and Wren calls it embellishing.

relationships.label: the second name on the list
relationships.note: She was the one who told him he was second on the list the Confessors read out in Coldmere.

relationships.label: the carter whose news she ran down to the hall
relationships.note: It was Rae who heard the list read at Coldmere and climbed through the night with it; Wren carried it the last of the way, from the winch-brothers and the kitchen to the infirmary hall.

deeper: The count never stops, even when she sleeps.
